const int MOD1 = 998244353;
const int MOD2 = 1000000007;
const int BASE = 1000000;

template<typename T> void read(T &x){

    for(; isdigit(c); c = getchar()) x = (x << 1) + (x << 3) + c - '0';
    x *= f;
}

ll n;
vector<int> tab[10];
ll gg;
int sum[10];
int ans;

void init() {
    struct Node { int u, x, nxt; };
    stack<Node> st;
    st.push({0, 0, 0});
    while (!st.empty()) {
        Node cur = st.top(); st.pop();
        int u = cur.u, x = cur.x, nxt = cur.nxt;
        if (nxt == 0) {
            tab[u].push_back(((++gg) - x + MOD1) % MOD1);
            sum[u] = (sum[u] + tab[u].back() % MOD2) % MOD2;
        }
        if (u == 6) continue;
        if (nxt < 10) {
            st.push({u, x, nxt + 1});
            st.push({u + 1, 10 * x + nxt, 0});
        }
    }
}

void solve(ll x) {
    stack<tuple<ll,int,int,int>> st; // x, state, next_digit?
    // state: 0 = first visit, 1 = after processing a child, etc.
    // We'll use explicit state to handle the block condition.
    st.emplace(x, 0, 0, 0); // (x, phase, dummy, dummy)
    while (!st.empty()) {
        auto [cur, phase, _, __] = st.top(); st.pop();
        if (phase == 0) {
            if (cur > n) continue;
            // Check block condition
            if (cur * BASE + BASE - 1 <= n && cur * BASE * 10 > n) {
                ll rk = gg;
                for (int i = 0, bit = 1; i <= 6; ++i, bit *= 10) {
                    int mae = ((rk - cur * bit) % MOD1 + MOD1) % MOD1;
                    int pos = lower_bound(tab[i].begin(), tab[i].end(), -mae + MOD1) - tab[i].begin();
                    ans = (ans + ( (1LL * mae * tab[i].size() % MOD2 + sum[i]) % MOD2 - 1LL * (tab[i].size() - pos) * MOD1 % MOD2 + MOD2) % MOD2) % MOD2;
                    gg += tab[i].size();
                }
                continue; // block processed, no further recursion
            }
            // single number
            ans = (ans + ((++gg) - cur + MOD1) % MOD1) % MOD2;
            // push state to process children (digits 0..9)
            st.emplace(cur, 1, 0, 9); // state 1, next_digit = 0, last = 9
            // Actually we need to process digits in order 0..9.
            // We'll push a special marker to iterate.
            // Simpler: push a task to process children iteratively.

            // Alternative: use a different approach: push all children in reverse order.
            // For state 0 we already processed current node. For children, we'll push them now in reverse.

            // To preserve order, push children in reverse order: 9..0.
            for (int d = 9; d >= 0; --d) {
